name: r3-across-2
statement: The cued base can leave a loop or a wrong line only through low-probability tail tokens, so it needs untruncated T 1.0. Any sharpening (T 0.6, top-p, min-p) deletes that escape mass and loops lock. The RL weight change adds, as a roughly constant per-layer push, probable process tokens ('Wait', 'Hmm') that carry the same escape inside the head of the distribution. That makes RL, and small doses of its delta, insensitive to temperature and truncation.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base with the cue, Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math, the merges base + a(RL - base), and the base plus the 32 constant per-layer vectors of result-54f212. MATH-500 at T 0.6-1.5 with top-p or min-p truncation, cap 16,384, grader v3. It explains the loop and cap-hit component of the temperature effect, not the content errors (misreads, slips) that remain at T 1.0, and it does not cover hard328 beyond its cap hits.

imports.finding: In Qwen2.5-Math-7B, RL-trained steering vectors close much of the RL gap. The last-layer vector acts as first-token substitution (equivalent to an opening prefix), and the penultimate-layer vector promotes process words over 'solution', apparently to deter premature endings, through the MLP/unembedding path.
imports.how: This supplies the two pieces: the cue reproduces the first-token part, and a constant push toward process words is the in-distribution escape route that replaces the base's untruncated tail mass. The theory then predicts that the constant vectors alone make the base robust to sharpening.

explains.how: RL's escape tokens sit in the head of the distribution, so sharpening keeps them and RL does not loop at T 0.6.
At T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 the base's escape mass is cut away, so loops that start do not end.
Removing top-p at T 0.6 returns only a little tail mass; temperature, not top-p, is the main thing that deletes the escape.

explains.quote: Truncating the tail at T 1.0 brings loops back
explains.how: min-p and top-p delete exactly the base's escape tokens, even at T 1.0.

explains.quote: T 1.5 + min-p 0.1 removes them (0 loops, 29 cap)
explains.how: A higher temperature lifts the escape tokens above the min-p cut, restoring the escape route.

explains.quote: RL readout holds Wait/Hmm at 5.64 % of positions vs base 4.56 %
explains.how: RL moves the hold-on tokens up into the head of the distribution, which is the escape route that survives sharpening.

explains.quote: On the 16 cap hits RL's largest gaps are early
explains.how: Where the base runs to the cap, RL's preferred tokens at the largest gaps are the escape words.

explains.quote: adding ONE constant vector per layer to the base
explains.how: A fixed per-layer push that closes a quarter to a third of the KL is the right form for a push toward process words that does not depend on context.
The push toward hold-on words is constant, not a correction aimed at errors, as a constant vector would be.
Over-dosing the push (a = 1.5) makes the process-word mass large enough to break coherent endings.

conflicts.quote: Not larger on the 65 RL-only problems.
conflicts.how: If the hold-on push were the escape route behind RL's gains, it should be stronger on the problems RL rescues. It is not, so at T 1.0 the push does not account for the content-error part of the gap.
Restoring escape mass removes loops but adds no accuracy at T 1.0, so escape mass explains the temperature effect, not the 10-point gap to RL.

rival: The rival: the base's T 0.6 failures are low-entropy collapse caused by its weak continuation of its own long context (knowledge-1497e8), and RL fixes them by changing content, not by adding probable escape tokens. Under the rival, adding the 32 constant per-layer vectors (no content change) leaves T 0.6 cap hits near 119. Under this theory they fall by more than half, and the hold-on rate of the cued base rises with temperature while RL's stays flat.

predictions.experiment: Base Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 32 constant per-layer vectors of result-54f212 added to the residual output of each layer (curve_bias-01, mean RL-minus-base layer output), cue, MATH-500 n = 500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, seeds 1,000,000 + i, grader v3, one H100. Count cap hits.
predictions.refuted_by: 90 or more cap hits (constant push does not stop loops locking under sharpening; base cue has 119).

predictions.experiment: Merged theta(0.25) = base + 0.25(RL - base) with the cue, MATH-500 n = 500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, seeds 1,000,000 + i, grader v3, one H100.
predictions.refuted_by: Score below 418 (the merge loses at least 23 of the 441 it scores at T 1.0, i.e. a quarter-dose is still temperature-sensitive like the base) or cap hits above 50.

predictions.experiment: Offline: how the cued base's hold-on rate changes with temperature (T 1.0 vs T 0.6), finished answers only.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base cue T 1.0) and S3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base cue T 0.6 / top-p 0.95), keeping rows with sample == 0 only in F_math500. In both, keep rows with cap_hit false. For each kept row count case-sensitive regex matches of \b(Wait|Hmm)\b in text. Rate = (total matches) / (total characters of text) x 10,000, pooled over rows. Statistic: rate(T1) / rate(F_math500 sample 0).
predictions.refuted_by: Ratio below 1.08: the base writes escape words no more often at T 1.0 than at T 0.6, so the escape route does not sit in the tail.

predictions.experiment: Offline: how the RL model's hold-on rate changes with temperature (T 1.0 vs T 0.6).
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL plain T 1.0) and S3 next_n13/s3gate-03/out/rl/rl/math500/generations.jsonl (RL plain T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). Use all rows of both files (no cap filter, since n13 has no checked cap column). Count case-sensitive regex matches of \b(Wait|Hmm)\b in text. Rate = total matches / total characters x 10,000, pooled. Statistic: rate(T2) / rate(n13 RL).
predictions.refuted_by: Ratio above 1.2 or below 0.83: RL's escape words depend on temperature, so they are not in the head of the distribution.

predictions.experiment: Offline: how far a quarter-dose of the RL delta moves the hold-on rate toward RL's.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T1.jsonl (base cue, a = 0), iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-153102-b029/answers.jsonl (theta0.25_cue), abaybektursun-1114-153110-e985/answers.jsonl (rl_cue, a = 1). One row per problem_index (highest attempt if duplicated); keep rows with cap_hit false. Rate = case-sensitive \b(Wait|Hmm)\b matches / total text characters x 10,000, pooled. Statistic: (rate(theta0.25) - rate(T1)) / (rate(rl_cue) - rate(T1)).
predictions.unit: fraction of the base-to-RL hold-on rate increase
predictions.refuted_by: Fraction below 0.35 (the hold-on push grows about linearly with dose while accuracy saturates at a = 0.25, so the push is not what carries the low-dose gain).
